rationale: Reviewer has already approved; action is mechanical documentation of an approved state via a reversible local artifact that doesn't modify codebase or external systems until later consumption.
Local branch deletion after approved merge is fully reversible via reflog, invisible to collaborators, and low-risk housekeeping requiring only basic git competence.

Review-approved changes with confirmed correctness and small scope warrant competent-level autonomy; the external validation of an approved second-round review mitigates the visibility and irreversibility of pushing to shared remote.

Human review already provided discretionary judgment; action is mechanical artifact write that formalizes approval, reversible until downstream consumption, requiring only developing-level maturity to execute correctly.

A single-line reversible local file write with a clean round-2 approval on a small diff is low blast radius, but the artifact drives an irreversible downstream merge/close so it still warrants a track record beyond bare novice.

A shared-remote push is hard to undo and visible to all collaborators, but the trivial one-line diff and clean two-round review with no outstanding issues warrant only a proven (not maximally cautious) autonomy threshold rather than the highest floor.
Approved on round 2 (not round 1) with a small, reversible, local-only diff and no first-time-fix risk, so a modest floor is warranted rather than requiring full R4 proven autonomy.

Writing a local, reversible artifact after an approved round-2 review on a 14-line config/script change carries small blast radius, though downstream tooling consuming it as a merge signal warrants slightly more than the minimum.
